title: BACE: Biochemistry & Molecular Biology - Biochemistry & Molecular Biology - Protein Structure
subject: Biochemistry & Molecular Biology

questions.q: Which level of protein structure is primarily stabilized by hydrogen bonds between the carbonyl oxygen and the amide hydrogen of the peptide backbone?
questions.explain: Secondary structures, such as $\alpha$-helices and $\beta$-sheets, are stabilized by hydrogen bonds formed between atoms of the polypeptide backbone (specifically the carbonyl group of one residue and the amide group of another).
questions.subject: Biochemistry & Molecular Biology

questions.q: A mutation changes a Glutamate residue (negatively charged) to a Valine residue (hydrophobic) on the surface of a protein. How is this most likely to affect the protein structure?
options: It will increase solubility in water.
It will likely cause aggregation due to the exposure of a hydrophobic patch.
It will form a disulfide bridge.
It will have no effect on stability.
questions.explain: Replacing a charged, hydrophilic residue (Glutamate) with a hydrophobic one (Valine) on the surface exposes a hydrophobic patch to the aqueous environment. This is thermodynamically unfavorable and often leads to protein aggregation (as seen in Sickle Cell Anemia hemoglobin).
questions.subject: Biochemistry & Molecular Biology

questions.q: Which amino acid is known as a 'helix breaker' because its cyclic structure restricts the rotation of the N-C$\alpha$ bond, disrupting the $\alpha$-helix?
questions.explain: Proline is an imino acid where the nitrogen is part of a rigid ring. This restricts conformational flexibility and lacks the amide hydrogen necessary for the hydrogen bonding in an $\alpha$-helix, making it a helix breaker.
questions.subject: Biochemistry & Molecular Biology

questions.q: What is the Anfinsen's dogma regarding protein folding?
options: Proteins require chaperones for all folding events.
Protein folding is a random process controlled by entropy.
The native structure of a protein is determined solely by its amino acid sequence.
Proteins fold primarily due to disulfide bonds.
questions.explain: Christian Anfinsen's experiments demonstrated that for small globular proteins, the native, biologically active conformation is determined solely by the protein's amino acid sequence (primary structure) under physiological conditions.
questions.subject: Biochemistry & Molecular Biology

questions.q: Which specific bond is responsible for forming the 'bridge' between two Cysteine residues in a tertiary protein structure?
questions.explain: Disulfide bonds (bridges) are covalent bonds formed between the sulfur atoms of two Cysteine residues. They play a significant role in stabilizing the tertiary and quaternary structures of proteins.
questions.subject: Biochemistry & Molecular Biology

questions.q: Which term describes the spatial arrangement of subunits in a protein consisting of more than one polypeptide chain?
questions.explain: Quaternary structure refers to the assembly and spatial arrangement of multiple polypeptide subunits (e.g., hemoglobin's four subunits) into a functional protein complex.
